question: Does an AI anomaly model with independent novelty and learned response-profile evidence improve over the failed DVWA v1 correlation model in a fresh controlled session?
data: Local DVWA at v1 pinned commit, traced process/connect/openat data plus HTTP response structure; single sequential PHP server, loopback only.
development: 1400 benign-only requests with seed 2026112601, first 70% for fit and baseline profiles, last 30% for threshold calibration; no attack telemetry before freeze.
test: Fresh session using different seeds, 500 benign requests and 30 attempts per previously known family, assessed once after SHA-256 freeze. Prior v1 experiment informed feature design; family novelty is NOT claimed.
model: IsolationForest fit on v1 correlated numerical features plus explicitly scored novelty for previously unseen executables/endpoints/files and per-path response-structure divergence learned from benign training only.
calibration: Benign-only 0.5% quantile; no change after viewing test. Unknown attack outcomes are not treated as success.
limitations: Synthetic local lab, known families, network/process traces joined using PHP single-thread assumption; not equivalent to operational unknown attack detection.
results: Pending execution; no outcome may be claimed before CI artifact is reviewed.
